Uniform precedent, Protocol-limb form (six entries): D-318 '…no observationsNotFindings field; they travel as honesty work.'; D-317 identical; D-316 identical; D-312 identical; D-311 identical; D-308 identical. Every one of these recites named Claude Stage B turn-1 observations and closes the enumeration with the standing clause.

Uniform precedent, Decision-limb form (three entries): D-313 'Claude Stage B turn-1 observations CLAUDE-D313-O1 … CLAUDE-D313-O5 travel as honesty work.'; D-310 '… CLAUDE-D310-O4 travel as honesty work.'; D-303 'Claude Stage B turn-1 observations CLAUDE-D303-O1 … CLAUDE-D303-O4 travel as honesty work.'

The nearest precedents are exact structural twins of this entry and dispose of the obvious rebuttal. D-317 and D-318 recite Stage B turn-1 observations whose members are id, observation, severity, where, whyItDoesNotStand — the same member set as here, including whyItDoesNotStand — and still record 'they travel as honesty work'. A whyItDoesNotStand member inside the review is therefore not treated by this corpus as a substitute for the entry's own standing clause.

The only counter-precedent I could find is D-296, which recites Stage B turn-2 observationsNotFindings without a standing clause — but those were four UNLABELED objects carrying no identifiers, so no identifier was left dangling. It does not reach a case where identifiers are named.

The subject's own line-5 assurance is about naming, not standing: 'All identifiers are named. No identifier is invented.' It makes no claim that every named identifier carries a disposition, and here three do not.
shouldFix.impact: COORD would carry three named identifiers with no recorded standing — the first entry in the D-303..D-318 run to do so. A later reader auditing D-319's identifier inventory finds CLAUDE-D319-O1..O3 named, shaped, and dispositionless, and cannot tell from the entry whether they were considered and set aside or silently dropped. The distinction the corpus maintains between a finding that lands and an observation that travels as honesty work is exactly what the missing clause records.

The Decision-limb form of D-303/D-310/D-313 would serve equally.

The operative act is untouched. The true standing is bound at a pinned, resolvable site — each of the three carries a whyItDoesNotStand member in the turn-1 review whose sha256 the entry itself recites — so no dispatch attack succeeds through the gap. Same grade and rationale as CLAUDE-D319-S2, which was likewise a disposition-recitation defect over a separately-bound truth.

observations.where: line 5, the clause 'observations CLAUDE-D319-O1, CLAUDE-D319-O2, CLAUDE-D319-O3 have members … ; an empty mustFix list; …'
observations.observation: The turn-2 rewrite replaced the precedent verb ('Claude 2 Stage B turn-1 RETURNED 3 named observations objects … (members …); an empty mustFix list; …') with 'observations … HAVE members …; an empty mustFix list; …'. The semicolon enumeration now hangs grammatically off 'observations … have', so the literal reading attributes an empty mustFix list and a 2-member shouldFix list to the three observation objects rather than to the review that returned them.
observations.whyItDoesNotStand: No reader can attribute a mustFix list to an observation object; the intended attachment is recoverable from the impossibility of the literal reading, and every count in the enumeration is correct against the review's bytes. It is a syntactic slip, not a false measurement. It is noted because the repair required by CLAUDE-D319-T2-SF1 restores the precedent verb form and cures this at zero additional cost.
